answers.question: A Moon base runs at 30% oxygen. What does NASA testing cover?
answers.sentence: NASA's tests cover 13.6–22.2% oxygen, so 30.0% oxygen is beyond what was tested — we can only show the closest tests, not an answer for that condition.

nearest_evidence.text: Nearest evidence beyond BASS-II: Saffire V tests V-2 to V-4, 25.4–26.2% oxygen at 70.7–72.6 kPa and 20 cm/s flow — still below a 30%+ oxygen Moon cabin at 10.2 psi or less.
nearest_evidence.source: Urban et al., ICES 2021, Saffire IV/V paper, Table 1 (NTRS 20210011521)

answers.gravity_note: These tests were in microgravity, on the ISS or in Cygnus cargo ships in orbit. The Moon is about one-sixth Earth's gravity. Pressure is known for only 8 tests (Saffire I, Saffire II and Saffire IV/V: 70.7–100.0 kPa); the BASS-II tables give none, so a Moon-base condition is not covered by these tests.
